text: Sheikh Abdul Rashid, born on 19 August 1967 in Langate, is an Indian politician better known as Engineer Rashid, who currently serves as a member of the Lok Sabha representing the Baramulla constituency in Jammu and Kashmir. He is the founder and patron of the Jammu and Kashmir Awami Ittehad Party and is renowned for his speeches, earning the nickname "Pain of Al-Baen" (Plough), a symbol of the National Conference. Rashid obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in 1988 and a diploma in civil engineering in 1990. He worked for over a decade as an engineer with the Jammu and Kashmir Projects Construction Corporation, known for being a simple man who dressed in a Khan suit, used public transportation, and occasionally hitched rides on motor cycles. He entered politics in 2008 by winning the Langate constituency as an independent candidate in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly election and retained it in 2014. In 2005, he was arrested by the SOG in Srinagar for supporting militants, jailed for three months and 17 days, and charged with anti-national activities, held in Cargo, Humhama, and Raj bagh prisons; the charges were later dropped on humanitarian grounds after five months of custody, following a negotiation where he paid ₹1.14 lakhs. In August 2019, he was arrested under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) on terror funding charges and remained in jail, contesting the 2024 parliamentary election from jail and winning, though he did not attend parliament. In September 2024, he was granted interim bail until 2 October to campaign for the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly election, which was extended by the Patiala House Court, Delhi, until 12 October 2024, allowing him to witness the election results. His bail was further extended until 28 October 2024, after which he was sent back to jail following the expiry of interim bail. In October 2015, he was assaulted by BJP MLAs in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly for hosting a party where beef was served on government premises to oppose the central government's beef ban, and a day later, he was attacked with black ink by BJP cadets at the Press Club New Delhi in response to his criticism of the lynching of a Kashmiri truck driver in Udhampur. Rashid defeated former and current Chief Minister Omar Abdullah in the 2024 Lok Sabha election from Baramulla.
